title: Bleach bypass & cross process
summary: Two film-lab looks: bleach bypass (silver left in, so a muted, harsh, high-contrast image) and cross processing (slide film in negative chemistry, with skewed colors and yellow highlights).

title: Brightness & contrast
summary: The everyday image adjustments: brightness, contrast, saturation and vibrance, applied to display-encoded values so the sliders behave like a photo editor’s.

title: Channel mixer
summary: Builds each output channel from a weighted mix of the input red, green and blue: swap channels, fake infrared, or make a custom black and white.

title: Color balance (lift, gamma, gain)
summary: The three wheels of a grading tool: lift tints the shadows, gamma the midtones and gain the highlights, per channel.

title: Curves
summary: Tone curves like a photo editor’s: a master curve for contrast and one curve per channel for color, through smooth points that never overshoot.

title: Exposure & gamma
summary: Exposure in photographic stops, a black-level offset and a gamma curve, applied in linear light before tone mapping, like adjusting a camera rather than a screenshot.

title: Gradient map
summary: Replaces every pixel with a color from a three-stop gradient chosen by its brightness, for thermal-camera, neon or tinted-print looks.

title: Hue / saturation
summary: Rotates hues, scales saturation and lifts or lowers lightness in OKLCH, a perceptual space, so a hue shift does not make yellows glow or blues go dark.

title: Invert / threshold
summary: A photographic negative, or a black-and-white threshold with an adjustable level and edge softness, optionally per channel for a posterized look.

title: Levels
summary: Photo-editor levels: stretch the tones between an input black and white point, bend the midtones with gamma, and remap to an output range, for all channels or one.

title: LUT color grading
summary: Grades the image through a 3D lookup table, such as a `.cube` file exported from Resolve, Premiere or Photoshop, with tetrahedral interpolation.

title: Monochrome
summary: Greyscale, classic sepia, or a duotone that maps shadows and highlights to two colors.

title: Split toning
summary: Tints the shadows with one color and the highlights with another, keeping brightness, like a darkroom split tone or a modern teal-and-orange grade.

title: Vignette
summary: Darkens or tints the frame toward its edges, drawing the eye to the center.

title: White balance
summary: Camera-style white balance: tell it the color temperature of the light and it neutralizes it (a Bradford adaptation in linear light), with a green–magenta tint.

title: Anamorphic streaks
summary: Stretches bright lights into long horizontal lines, the blue flares of anamorphic cinema lenses.

title: Chromatic aberration
summary: Shifts red and blue (or a whole spectrum) apart, like a lens that focuses each wavelength at a slightly different place.

title: Depth of field
summary: Blurs what is nearer or farther than the focus distance, as a wide-aperture lens does.

title: Film grain
summary: Photographic grain: fine noise that sits mostly in shadows and midtones and changes at a film frame rate.

title: Fisheye & Panini
summary: Re-projects the perspective frame: an equidistant fisheye that bulges the center, or a Panini projection that keeps verticals straight and widens the view without stretching the edges.

title: Halation
summary: The red-orange glow around bright lights on film, where light bounced off the film base and exposed the red layer again.

title: Lens dirt
summary: Smudges, dust and rings on the lens that only show where bright light spreads across them, like a dirty camera pointed at the sun.

title: Lens distortion
summary: Barrel, pincushion or mustache distortion from the Brown–Conrady radial lens model, with a choice of what fills the edges.

title: Lens flare
summary: Ghost reflections and a halo mirrored through the frame center from every bright spot, with color fringes, a starburst and lens dirt, as light bounces inside a camera lens.

title: Motion blur
summary: Blurs moving objects and camera motion along their path, as a camera shutter does.

title: Tilt-shift
summary: The miniature-model look of a tilted lens: a sharp band of focus, with blur growing smoothly on either side.

title: Bloom
summary: Light bleeding around bright areas.

title: Blur
summary: Blurs the whole frame with a separable Gaussian, a box filter, or iterated Kawase passes, optionally at reduced resolution for wide, cheap blurs.

title: Bokeh blur
summary: Blurs the whole frame through a round or hexagonal aperture, so highlights turn into soft discs or hexagons.

title: Directional blur
summary: Smears the image along one direction, like a fast camera pan or a streak of speed.

title: Frosted glass
summary: Looks through a pane of frosted glass: a backdrop blur with ripples, a tint and fine grain, matching HoloCSS’s Glass theme.

title: Glow
summary: A soft colored halo around selected objects, like an outer glow in an image editor.

title: Radial & zoom blur
summary: Blurs toward or around a center point: a zoom burst that rushes at the viewer, or a spin like a rotating camera.

title: Selective bloom
summary: Bloom from selected objects only: give it a selection or texture mask and just those pixels feed the glow, which still spreads over everything around them.

title: Star filter
summary: Turns highlights into stars with two, three or more crossing streaks, like a star filter screwed onto a lens.

title: Bit crush
summary: Throws away color depth (and optionally resolution), like a frame buffer with too few bits: smooth gradients turn into bands.

title: Block displacement
summary: Corrupted-video blocks: random rectangles of the image jump sideways, with a little channel separation.

title: Datamosh
summary: The look of a video with its keyframes removed: motion drags the old picture along in blocks, smearing it into the new one until the next keyframe resets it.

title: Digital noise
summary: Video static: mono or color noise that changes every frame, with occasional stronger horizontal bands.

title: JPEG artifacts
summary: Compresses each frame the way JPEG does (8×8 DCT blocks quantized with the standard tables, color at quarter resolution) and decodes it again, for blocky, ringing, smeared-color artifacts at low quality.

title: Pixel sort
summary: Sorts runs of pixels by brightness or hue along rows or columns, the glitch-art streaks of pixel sorting.

title: RGB split glitch
summary: Red and blue jump apart in quick, seeded steps, like a misaligned digital signal.

title: Scanline tear
summary: Bands of scanlines slip sideways and wrap around, with an optional sinusoidal wobble, like a TV losing horizontal sync.

title: Signal loss
summary: Brief digital dropouts: now and then the picture freezes on its last good frame (or falls to noise), torn by bands of static, then recovers.

title: Slice shift
summary: Cuts the frame into horizontal (or vertical) slices that slide out of line by random amounts, re-cutting a few times a second.

title: ASCII
summary: Redraws the image as text: each cell becomes the character whose ink matches its brightness, in the original colors or in two theme colors.

title: CRT
summary: A cathode-ray tube: curved glass, an aperture-grille, slot or shadow mask, scanlines, phosphor glow, a vignette and a slight flicker.

title: Dither
summary: Reduces each channel to a few levels and hides the banding with a dither pattern: ordered Bayer matrices, void-and-cluster blue noise, or interleaved gradient noise.

title: Error-diffusion dither
summary: The organic dither of Floyd–Steinberg and of the classic Mac’s Atkinson, approximated on the GPU in 4×4 tiles: few colors, with the rounding error spread to neighboring pixels.

title: Halftone
summary: Print-style halftone screens: four rotated CMYK screens, a single ink, or additive RGB, drawn as dots, lines or squares sized by the tone under each cell.

title: LCD subpixels
summary: A macro view of an LCD: every pixel is three red, green and blue stripes with dark gaps, and slow pixels leave ghosts behind moving things.

title: NTSC composite
summary: Sends the image through a simulated composite video signal and back: soft color, crawling dots along edges and rainbow artifacts in fine detail, like a game console on an old TV.

title: Palette reduction
summary: Repaints the image with only the colors of a classic palette (Game Boy, CGA, EGA, PICO-8, Commodore 64, NES, or four of your own), matched by perceived difference, with optional dithering.

title: Pixelate
summary: Big square, hexagonal or round pixels, each the color at its center.

title: Scanlines
summary: Darkened horizontal or vertical lines across the frame, hard or soft, optionally scrolling slowly.

title: Teletext
summary: Rebuilds the image from teletext block graphics: a 40×25 grid of cells, each a 2×3 mosaic in two of eight broadcast colors, or 1-bit white on black.

title: VHS
summary: A worn VHS tape: wobbling lines, colors bleeding to the right of edges, a rolling tracking band, head-switching noise at the bottom and a PLAY display with a tape counter.

title: Crosshatch
summary: Redraws the image in pen-and-ink hatching: darker areas get more layers of crossing lines.

title: Edge detect (Sobel, Canny)
summary: Finds edges in the image itself (not the 3D geometry, unlike outline): Sobel gradients of brightness, optionally thinned to one-pixel lines as Canny does, over the image, on paper, or glowing on black.

title: Emboss
summary: Presses the image into a relief lit from one side: edges facing the light rise, the others sink.

title: Kuwahara (painterly)
summary: An edge-preserving smoothing filter that turns detail into flat, brushy patches, like an oil painting: each pixel takes the calmest neighboring region’s average.

title: Mosaic & stained glass
summary: Breaks the image into irregular cells (a Voronoi mosaic), each filled with one color and outlined in lead, like stained glass or tiles.

title: Outline
summary: Draws lines where the depth or the surface direction changes, for a toon or technical-drawing look.

title: Pencil sketch
summary: Redraws the scene as a pencil sketch on paper: contours from the geometry (depth and normals) and the image, and shading in diagonal strokes that pile up in the shadows.

title: Toon posterize
summary: Flattens brightness into a few bands while keeping each color’s hue, and darkens edges, for a cartoon look on any image.

title: Watercolor
summary: Paints the image in watercolor: soft washes that bleed and waver, darker rims where pigment pools, and grain where it settles into the paper.

title: Bulge & pinch
summary: A round lens that magnifies the image toward its center (bulge) or squeezes it (pinch).

title: Displacement map
summary: Offsets the image by the values of a texture, scaled and scrolling: red and green move pixels sideways and up, or brightness moves them along an angle.

title: Liquid flow warp
summary: Swirls the image through a slowly changing flow field (curl noise), so it moves like ink in water without tearing.

title: Heat haze
summary: The shimmer of hot air: the image wobbles in small, rising ripples, strongest near the bottom.

title: Kaleidoscope
summary: Folds the frame into mirrored wedges around a point, like looking through a kaleidoscope.

title: Mirror
summary: Reflects one side of the frame onto the other across a vertical or horizontal line (or both, for four-way symmetry).

title: Ripple
summary: Concentric water ripples, or a shockwave ring that expands and fades, spreading from a point.

title: Twirl
summary: Twists the image around a point like a whirlpool: strongest at the center and fading out by the edge of the radius.

title: Wave warp
summary: Bends the image along travelling sine waves, horizontally, vertically or both, like a flag in the wind or a reflection in water.

title: Depth fog
summary: Screen-space fog from the depth buffer: linear or exponential with distance, optionally thinning above a height for ground mist.

title: God rays
summary: Light shafts that stream from a light past the objects in front of it, as sunbeams through dusty air.

title: Screen-space rim light
summary: Adds a rim light to every object’s silhouette from the depth and normal buffers, like a backlight separating subjects from the background, without touching materials.

title: Ambient occlusion (SSAO)
summary: Darkens creases, corners and contact points where ambient light is blocked, from a normal-oriented hemisphere of samples around each pixel.

title: Volumetric fog
summary: Fog with volume: rays march from the camera through height fog that drifts with noise, collecting light scattered toward the viewer (stronger looking toward the light).

title: Holographic foil material
summary: The holographic foil as a material: the rainbow and glints follow the true viewing angle at each point of the surface, so a card, sticker or logo shimmers as it or the camera moves, with no pointer input needed.

title: Glitter
summary: Scatters tiny tilted flakes over surfaces that catch the light one by one, so they twinkle as the light sweeps or the pointer moves.

title: Hologram
summary: Turns a mesh into a projected hologram: see-through additive light with moving scanlines, a bright fresnel rim, a gentle flicker and occasional glitch slices.

title: Holographic foil
summary: An iridescent rainbow sheen, like a holographic trading card.

title: HUD grid
summary: A holographic heads-up overlay in the accent color: a fine grid with brighter major lines, corner brackets around the frame, and a slow scan sweep.

title: Moiré interference
summary: Overlays two fine line or ring patterns at a slight angle, so they interfere into the large, shifting bands of moiré, as in security holograms and layered screens.

title: Prism dispersion
summary: Splits the image into a full spectrum fanning out from a center, so edges grow rainbow fringes like light through a prism or a cheap lens.

title: Thin-film iridescence
summary: Soap-bubble and oil-slick colors from thin-film interference: a film whose thickness varies across the surface reflects different wavelengths, and the colors slide as the viewing angle changes.

title: Chromatic fresnel rim
summary: Lights the rim of a surface in a full spectrum, violet to red across its width, like dispersive glass or a soap film at grazing angles.

title: Dissolve
summary: Burns the surface away as `progress` goes from 0 to 1, in noisy patches or as a front sweeping up the object, with a glowing edge.

title: Force field
summary: Turns a mesh (best a sphere or capsule) into a translucent energy shield: a glowing rim, a hexagon lattice that lights up toward the edges, and ripples that spread from a hit.

title: Fresnel glow
summary: Adds light where a surface turns away from the camera, the rim lighting of force fields, energy shields and selected objects.

title: Matcap swap
summary: Shades any material from a matcap: a picture of a lit sphere looked up by the surface direction, for clay, chrome or candy looks without lights.

title: Pearlescent & opal
summary: A pale, glowing sheen that shifts hue as the surface turns away and varies from flake to flake, like pearl, opal or pearlescent car paint.

title: Toon shading
summary: Cel shading on any lit material: the light snaps into flat bands (or follows a ramp you draw) while each surface keeps its color, the highlight becomes one flat spot, and an optional hard rim outlines the silhouette.

title: Triplanar mapping
summary: Wraps a texture around any shape without UVs: it is projected along the three axes and blended by how much the surface faces each, in world space (so it stays put while objects move) or object space (so it moves with them).

title: Wireframe glow
summary: Draws glowing lines along every triangle edge at a constant width on screen, over a faint fill or nothing at all.

title: Vertex wobble
summary: Makes surfaces breathe and wobble: vertices move along their normals by slowly drifting noise, and the normals are recomputed so lighting follows the new shape.

title: X-ray
summary: Turns a surface into a see-through shell of light, brightest at its edges, that shows through whatever is in front of it.

title: Burn
summary: Burns the image away in noisy patches: the paper chars ahead of a glowing edge in the theme accent, and the next image shows through behind it.

title: Crossfade & luma wipe
summary: Blends to the next image everywhere at once, through noise, or along a luma pattern (linear, radial, diamond or spiral) with a soft edge that can glow in the theme accent.

title: Glitch cut
summary: Cuts to the next image through digital damage: blocks flip over one by one around the middle while slices shift and the color channels split.

title: Holographic sweep
summary: A band of rainbow light sweeps across like a hologram catching the light, bending the image as it passes and leaving the next image behind it.

title: Morph
summary: Flows one image into the next along a displacement field: the old image is pushed away as it fades while the new one settles into place.

title: Pixelate transition
summary: Breaks the image into ever larger blocks, switches to the next image at the coarsest point, then sharpens back down to single pixels.

title: Pixel-sort wipe
summary: A wipe with a glitch-art edge: behind the moving front, each line of the next image appears sorted by brightness, as if a pixel sort were running along the direction of travel, before it settles into the image.

title: Wipe
summary: Reveals the next image behind a moving edge: a straight line at any angle, a circle growing from a center, or a clock hand sweeping around it.

title: Zoom / warp speed
summary: Rushes into the image with radial speed streaks from a center, then the next image arrives out of the same streaks and settles to its size.

title: Buffer view
summary: Shows a geometry buffer instead of the image: distance from the camera, view-space normals from the prepass or reconstructed from depth, world position, screen-space motion, or the mask given to this effect.
